memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
The LORD said to Moses, "Speak to the Israelites and say to them:
'These are my appointed festivals, the appointed festivals of the LORD,
which you are to proclaim as sacred assemblies'" - Lev 23:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice the small word that changes everything: my. These are not
Israel's festivals that God graciously agreed to attend. They are His
appointed times, and He invites His people into them.

The Hebrew word behind "appointed festivals" carries the sense of a
fixed meeting time. God was putting appointments in the calendar of a
whole nation. Twice a year, three times a year, once a week - come and
meet with Me.

Dear friend, think about what that says. The God of the universe wanted
regular, scheduled time with His people. He did not leave it to
whenever they felt spiritual. He wrote it into the year.

We often treat time with God as something that happens if the day
allows it. But love that is real usually shows up in the diary. We make
appointments for what matters to us.

Jesus, who was fully God, still rose early and went to a solitary place
to pray (Mark 1:35). If He kept appointments with the Father, how much
more do we need them?

Look at your week honestly. Where is your appointed time with God? Not
out of duty, but because He has invited you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I have a regular, protected time with God, or only leftovers?
2. What does my calendar reveal about what I truly value?
3. How would I feel if a friend treated our meetings the way I treat
   time with God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that You want time with me. Help me to guard that
time and to come to it gladly, not out of duty. Amen.
